report_title: On the Reproducibility of: "Learning Perturbations to Explain Time Series Predictions"
authors: Wouter Bant; Ádám Divák; Jasper Eppink; Floris Six Dijkstra
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2023/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
original_title: Learning Perturbations to Explain Time Series Predictions (ExtremalMask)
verdict_prose: despite notable discrepancies in results across many experiments, proposed method consistently outperforms all baselines; HOWEVER visualizations for the preservation game reveal learned perturbations primarily resemble a constant zero signal, questioning the importance of learning perturbations; revised deletion game sometimes surpasses preservation game
per_claim: SOTA claim=SUPPORTED (with discrepancies); learnable-perturbation mechanism=QUESTIONED (zero signal); NOTE second reproduction of same original as fCNqD2IuoD (more positive) - witness disagreement

report_title: "Studying How to Efficiently and Effectively Guide Models with Explanations" - A Reproducibility Study
authors: Adrian Sauter; Milan Miletić; Ryan Ott; Rohith Saai Pemmasani Prabakaran
original_title: Studying How to Efficiently and Effectively Guide Models with Explanations
verdict_prose: the major part of the original work is reproducible, with certain minor exceptions; extensions: EPG metric has robustness issue and bbox-size bias; Energy loss guides to on-object features without segmentation masks; contextual cues matter in certain scenarios
per_claim: major part=REPRODUCED; minor exceptions exist; metric critique is an extension

authors: Oliver Bentham; Nathan Stringham; Ana Marasovic
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2023/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
original_title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (CoT dependence metric)
verdict_prose: under specific conditions, successfully reproduce the scaling-then-inverse-scaling trends for CoT faithfulness on three model families; HOWEVER after normalizing for answer-choice bias, unfaithfulness drops significantly for smaller models, and the normalized metric correlates with accuracy (R^2=0.74), raising doubts about its validity
per_claim: scaling trends=REPRODUCED under specific conditions; metric validity=CHALLENGED (correlated with accuracy)
